clue.text: Most shoddy copier parts bust

indicators.note: the copier parts the bust, splitting it open to sit in the middle

parts.note: a bust is the chest
an ape is one who copies or mimics

explanation.surface: A broken-down office photocopier is the worst-quality machine around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copier' reads as an office machine, but it is a mimic, the APE.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoddy goods are cheaply made, so the shoddiest are the least costly ones.

clue.text: African oil's fluid state

indicators.note: fluid means flowing and shifting, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of African oil; the 's is 'is', a link

explanation.surface: African oil in liquid form.
explanation.definitionFit: A US state on the Pacific coast.

clue.text: Decapitated nimble little creature

indicators.note: decapitated means the head, the first letter, is removed

parts.note: deft means nimble

explanation.surface: A quick small animal has lost its head.
explanation.definitionFit: A newt, especially a young one, is a small amphibian creature.

clue.text: Overtly trendy Liberal introduced to sport

indicators.note: introduced to means set inside the word for sport

parts.note: to sport is to play
in means fashionable, trendy

explanation.surface: A fashionable Liberal politician openly takes up a sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Clearly and openly, without disguise, is done overtly.

clue.text: Cutting tweet about charmer not in good taste

indicators.note: about means the word for tweet goes around the charmer

parts.note: birds tweet, that is, sing
a witch casts charms
off means gone bad, and also inappropriate

explanation.surface: A cutting tweet about a seducer is in poor taste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tweet' suggests social media, but it is birdsong.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutting the power to a device means turning it off.

clue.text: Outdated measure reduced assistance on public transport

indicators.note: on means the shortened assistance comes after the transport in this across answer

parts.note: a bus is public transport

indicators.note: reduced means the word for assistance is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: help is assistance

explanation.surface: A complaint that help on buses has been cut back.
explanation.walkthrough: A bushel is an old imperial unit of dry volume, about eight gallons.
explanation.definitionFit: An old imperial unit of dry volume, about eight gallons, rarely used now.

clue.text: Wrinkle-free dancing nude holds nothing back

indicators.note: the shuffled nude holds, encloses, the reversed nothing
dancing means the letters move about
back means nothing is read backwards

parts.note: nil means nothing

explanation.surface: A nude dancer holds nothing back and has smooth skin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' makes UNED; the surface's 'holds nothing back' is the wordplay read literally.
explanation.definitionFit: Skin without lines or creases is smooth, free of wrinkles.

clue.text: Desolate ground with elevated height made public

indicators.note: elevated in a down clue means the letter for height is lifted to the top

parts.note: earth is ground
news is broken when made public

explanation.surface: A survey of a high plateau made public.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elevated' moves H from the end of EARTH to the top, giving HEART.
explanation.definitionFit: Desolate here is grief-stricken, utterly crushed by sorrow.

clue.text: Small section of notable estate remains

indicators.note: a small section of the phrase is concealed inside it

explanation.surface: Only a small part of a grand estate survives.
explanation.definitionFit: Sediment left at the bottom of a wine cask is the remains, the dregs.

clue.text: Profligate trio, with halo slipping

indicators.note: slipping suggests the letters slide out of place into a new order

explanation.surface: Three fallen angels whose haloes are slipping.
explanation.definitionFit: A seducer and rake, from a character in Rowe's play, is a dissolute, profligate man.

clue.text: First to cut up sticks, or stick

indicators.note: First to picks out the opening letter of the word cut

parts.note: to up sticks is to move away, to leave

explanation.surface: Advice to someone fed up: get out first, or stay stuck.
explanation.walkthrough: The word also means 'cut', a nice echo of the clue's first word.
explanation.definitionFit: To cleave to something is to adhere or cling to it, an older sense of stick.

clue.text: Only wearing blue, Conservative later accepted redundancy

indicators.note: wearing blue means the word for only is wrapped in blue
later accepted puts the Conservative letter late within the word for blue

parts.note: blue means smutty, obscene
sole means only

explanation.surface: A Tory dressed only in blue later took redundancy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blue' suggests the Tory colour but means smutty.
explanation.definitionFit: Becoming outdated and no longer needed is a state of redundancy.

clue.text: Trimming down executive body that's usually in office

definitions.note: elliptical: the thing that is usually found in an office

parts.note: filing down is trimming with a file
the Cabinet is the government's executive body

explanation.surface: A government is slimming down its executive, the ministers usually in office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in office' suggests ministers holding power; it means a piece of office furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawer unit for papers is standard furniture in a workplace office.

clue.text: Most unrestrained, rampant wild flower

parts.note: loosest means least restrained
rife means rampant, widespread

explanation.surface: A wild flower spreading with total abandon.
explanation.definitionFit: Purple and yellow varieties of this plant grow wild by rivers.

clue.text: Abandoned types cavort topless during rave-ups

indicators.note: during puts the shortened cavort inside the rave-ups

parts.note: flings are wild parties or sprees

indicators.note: topless removes the first letter in this down clue

parts.note: to bound is to leap and cavort

explanation.surface: Wild partygoers prance about topless at raves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abandoned' suggests wild behaviour but means deserted.
explanation.definitionFit: Infants left by unknown parents to be found by others are deserted children.

clue.text: Large track which cattle go back inside

indicators.note: inside places the reversed cattle sound within the track

parts.note: RY is short for railway, a track

indicators.note: back means the cattle's call is read in reverse

parts.note: cattle go moo

explanation.surface: A big droveway along which the herd heads home.
explanation.definitionFit: Spacious, with plenty of room, means large in size.

clue.text: So one might, like a friar perhaps, recall scriptures

parts.note: a friar belongs to a religious order, so is in an order

indicators.note: recall, calling back, says the scriptures abbreviation runs backwards

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, scriptures

explanation.surface: A friar is asked to recite scripture from memory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recall' looks like remembering but means calling back, a reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase introduces a purpose, much as 'so that one might' does.

clue.text: Hardliner's spoken of fancy diary

definitions.note: the 's is 'is', joining definition to wordplay

indicators.note: spoken of says the words are heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a fancy, or idea, plus a diary, a log

explanation.surface: A political hardliner is said to keep an elaborate journal.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctrinaire zealot rigidly committed to a creed is a hardliner.

clue.text: Runs away from ill-disposed Israelis and gets in touch

indicators.note: ill-disposed means badly arranged, so the remaining letters are shuffled
away from means the runs letter departs from the word

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Someone flees unfriendly Israelis and makes contact.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ill-disposed' reads as hostile but signals the anagram of ISAELIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting as a link and cooperating with others is making contact.

clue.text: Occupied, as an admirer may be

definitions.meaning: a seat or room in use is occupied
an admirer is captivated, smitten by someone

explanation.surface: A seat claimed, or a heart claimed by an admirer.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: a chair already spoken for, and a person charmed or smitten.

clue.text: We're told to consider religious faction equally split

indicators.note: we're told says the word for consider is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: to try a case is to consider it
a sect is a religious faction

explanation.surface: We're asked to weigh up a religious group divided evenly.
explanation.definitionFit: To divide into three equal parts is to split equally.

clue.text: Means of controlling the flow, primarily for sailing craft at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters are mixed up
primarily takes the opening letter of the word for

explanation.surface: Signals at sea controlling the movement of sailing boats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' shuffles F (from 'primarily for') with SAILINGCRAFT.
explanation.definitionFit: Road lights that stop and start vehicles regulate the flow of traffic.

clue.text: Fearful African leader to join Union

indicators.note: leader takes the opening letter of African

parts.note: to wed is to join in union, marriage

explanation.surface: A frightened African leader joining a union.
explanation.definitionFit: Filled with reverential dread, so fearful.

clue.text: All the time that's left in game

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation inside the card game

parts.note: whist is a card game

explanation.surface: How much time is left in a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'All the time' is the conjunction meaning 'during the whole time that'.
explanation.definitionFit: The conjunction means during the whole time that something happens.

clue.text: Junior to dash back to get support

parts.note: someone junior to another ranks under them

indicators.note: back means the word for dash is read backwards

parts.note: to nip is to dash quickly somewhere

explanation.surface: A junior is sent dashing back for reinforcements.
explanation.definitionFit: To shore up or strengthen from below is to support.

clue.text: Backing expert

explanation.surface: An expert providing support.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: for a cause, and a skilled professional.

clue.text: Like Beau, ignoring the odds, persist with dull clothing

indicators.note: the dull word clothes, wraps around, the even letters

parts.note: dry means dull, boring

indicators.note: ignoring the odds keeps only the even-placed letters of persist

explanation.surface: A dandy defies the odds by persisting with dull clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: Beau Brummell was the famous Regency dandy, noted for his elegant dress.
explanation.definitionFit: Beau Brummell was a byword for smart, elegant clothes, so stylishly turned out.

clue.text: Skilled American on reserve briefly in party

indicators.note: on places the American abbreviation next to the rest in this across entry
in puts the shortened reserve inside the party

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: briefly means the reserve word loses its last letter

parts.note: an extra is a reserve or spare

explanation.surface: A capable American is held in reserve at a party.
explanation.definitionFit: Adroit with the hands, deft and clever, means skilled.
